title: Asian governments react to Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s exit
lede: Governments across Asia responded to Jensen Huang's exit from Nvidia in different ways, from reconfirming GPU supply deals to watching local projects and defending their own investigations.

points: China's foreign ministry called the spying allegations against the businesswoman linked to Huang groundless and restated its opposition to export controls.
Reuters reports more than $3 billion of Chinese AI computing projects that rely on restricted Nvidia processors now face uncertainty.
Singapore says it held Alice Huang's passport in 2025 over suspected false server declarations, later warned and barred her, and its Megaspeed probe continues.
South Korea says Nvidia reaffirmed its plan to supply 260,000 advanced GPUs, and Taipei says Nvidia's planned overseas headquarters stays on track.
Japan's Industry Ministry will monitor Nvidia closely and stressed a stable chip supply.

sections.text: Much of the world's AI compute pipeline runs through Nvidia's Asian partners and state deals, so these statements signal whether GPU supply plans survive the leadership change.
